findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`, so the guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only calls hooks named `include_<attr>?`. The method here is `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code. `website_name` is therefore always serialized, even when the website is blank (it comes out as `nil`). The intended condition `website.present?` is never applied. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute (TL0/anonymous) restriction
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer). The new `website_name` is derived from the same value but is not in that list and has no equivalent guard. It is serialized unconditionally, so it leaks the host and path of the website of a user whose website is meant to be hidden. The template shows `model.website_name` whenever it is present, so the old behaviour (nothing displayed when `website` is hidden) changes. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or make its include check respect `restrict_user_fields?`.

findings.title: Profile website display no longer updates after the website is edited
findings.body: The template used to compute `websiteName` client-side from `model.website`, so it was always current. It now reads the server-supplied `model.website_name`. `User.save` only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response and never refreshes `website_name`. `preferences` is nested under the `user` route, so the user profile is not re-fetched when the user returns from editing. After changing the website, the profile header can show the old name, or nothing if there was no website before, until a full reload.

findings.title: Path handling gives odd output for trailing slashes and ignores case
findings.body: When the domains match, the result is `website_host + path`. For `http://example.com/` this yields `example.com/` with a stray trailing slash, and the user who typed the bare domain sees a different display. Host comparison is also case-sensitive: `URI` does not lowercase the host, so `http://Example.com/x` will not match `example.com`. Normalize with `downcase` and strip a lone `/`.

findings.title: Spec leaves the sibling-subdomain branch, nil/invalid URL and untrusted cases uncovered
findings.body: The new tests cover only the non-matching, exact-match and parent-domain cases. The middle branch (same-length hosts with a shared parent, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is untested. So are a website with no scheme or an unparsable URL (`website_name` is `nil`), a blank website, and the TL0-anonymous case. The existing `untrusted_attributes` list in the spec was not extended with `website_name`, which is why the leak described above goes unnoticed.
